nodes.summary: Everything above the carrier (the cursor, resuming, the stream, the calls) is the MCP adapter's; only `call_tool` and the listing differ.
The real broker client (`aiomqtt`, optional). On Windows it needs the selector event loop; Linux and the containers need nothing.
The part of a broker client the adapter needs: subscribe to some filters, then receive (topic, payload) pairs.
Holds readings per sensor and releases them in `sequence_no` order.
A timeline sink that keeps recent events and fans them out to connected screens.
Owns the running Brain behind the API: one scenario at a time, or a live connection.
The cassette has no recorded answer for this request.
A chat model that records its inner model's answers or plays them back.
The in-memory store, with every write copied to Neo4j.
High-impact calls (a valve, the grid). `off`: the gate holds them. `human`: they wait for a signed approval from a person.
What the department desks (Fire, Ambulance and medical, Traffic control, Disaster response, Utilities) may tell the public: the words are fixed here, never written by a model.
What one of the Brain's own actions is known to do to what a sensor reads, so the change is not a surprise.
How to build a field the Brain expects from one the Twin sends: `canonical = twin_field * scale + offset`.
How the Brain predicts a numeric sensor from its own history, and how far off a reading must be to count as a surprise.
One signing key of a peer. The first key listed for a peer is its current one.
How retrieval ranks. Both switches are off (0) by default, so the ranking is the plain fusion of the two searches.
Sleep: what may be compiled from episodes into reflexes, and how much.
Estimators that look ahead of a threshold.
The Brain's own MCP server (read-only tools for other teams' agents), mounted at `/mcp` on the API port.
The broker a Twin publishes readings to (adapter `mqtt`). Actions, topology and capabilities still go to `twin.url` over HTTP.
Where the Brain sends its spans. Metrics at `/metrics` need no setting; spans need a collector and the optional packages (`uv sync --extra otel`).
Solvers that return their answer with a certificate. All on (6 Nov); `brain baseline --plain` and the `--set` flags measure the Brain with them off.
The planning supervisor (a LangGraph graph with checkpoints). On: it opens the emergency corridor after a fire or ambulance dispatch.
Who may call the API. `auto` requires tokens only when the server listens off loopback (`brain serve` decides).

Files for TLS. As a client: `ca` is the authority to trust, `cert` and `key` what we present for mutual TLS. As a server: `cert` and `key` are ours, and `ca` (if set) is the authority a client's certificate must come from.
Scarce attention: how many incidents may ask the agent team for deliberation at once, and how they are ranked.
Common envelope carried by every actuator call (Data Dictionary section 1).
A person's approval of one high-impact call (extension): signed, bound to the call's parameters, used once.
How strongly the evidence ties one entity to one incident.
Data Dictionary section 5 (extended actuators).
Extension: one observation of one citizen.
What a rule or an agent wants done. Only the gate can turn it into a call.
Extension: stand a dispatched unit down and return it to its station.
Common envelope carried by every sensor reading (Data Dictionary section 1).
Data Dictionary section 4: hold a traffic signal in one phase for a while.
CloudEvents 1.0 JSON envelope. `traceid` ties an event to the reading that caused it.
Data Dictionary section 2: congestion and, when the camera sees it, smoke.
Guardian's answer to "is this reading telling the truth?" (agreed format).
Extension: feedback on a dispatched unit, so incidents can close.
A department, or pack: what it reads, may do and detects. Data, so a change of partner is a file edit.
Runs department teams as background tasks so the reading loop never waits on them.
The incident ended while its team was still deliberating: nothing is left to plan for.
What `Deliberations` runs for a desk: analyst, chief, verify, propose, gate, act, in that order.
Deterministic stand-ins: the same incident always gets the same assessment and the same decision.
Each role is a tool-calling agent (LangChain `create_agent`) with a structured final answer.
Deterministic stand-ins. They follow the playbook literally and never escalate past the rules.
The read-only tools one deliberation may use, and a log of every call made.
Picks a station for one dispatch by solving every open incident that wants the same kind of unit together.
Plans a shed for an overload: finds the feeder the overloaded zone is on, reads each zone's latest trusted load, and asks `shed`.
One thing that happened on the way to the decision, with the region of the Brain it belongs to (the canopy's region ids).
A knowledge base whose index stops answering after `fail_after_searches` searches.
Passes verdicts to a real Guardian adapter until it has given `after_verdicts`, then answers nothing (a verdict or a quarantine check).
Passes everything to a real Twin adapter, except that the Twin goes away for a while after `after_readings` readings.
The journal cannot be trusted: a line was changed, the chain is broken, or the seal does not match.
A GuardianPort that passes everything through and writes the Guardian's answers, and its silences, to the journal.
A TwinPort that passes everything through and writes what came in to the journal.
An item reached from a seed by walking links: which seed, which kind of walk, and the links it took.
One link on the way to a hit, in the direction it is really stored: `from_id` REL `to_id`.
How a search chose: what each signal ranked (id, rank from 1, score), what was set aside and why, and what was kept.

Remembers every vector it has made, in memory and in a file beside the model: the playbook is embedded on every scenario start and takes about eight seconds, so without this the first thing the screen does after a click is wait.
The same stories kept in Neo4j: `:Episode` nodes with an embedding, linked to the incident type, found by a vector index. The nodes hold the story and nothing else: no readings, no plans, no outcome.
Raised instead of a model call while the model is being left alone.
The real scoring battery. Everything in it is synthetic or a Test Book scenario: nothing is read from a live city.
Triage found new evidence for these incidents (or opened them).
One reading, parsed, with the Guardian's verdict on it. Published as soon as it is stored.
A timeline sink: it reads `brain.action.requested` and `brain.action.result` and never writes.
A timeline sink: it watches the Brain's own events and writes an episode when an incident closes.
A change the Brain's own action is known to cause: in this zone, in this kind of sensor and field, in this direction, in this window.
The units the log says are out, built event by event.
A value was proposed that is not on the surface, or is outside its range.
Answers like the scripted team, but at `rate` per role call it fails: an error, or a garbage answer.
The journal cannot be trusted, or the config it would run under is not the one it was recorded with.
`inproc_partners(...)`: use it as `async with`. Left without a transport, it takes the one the scenario names (`transport` in the file), else MCP.
A Twin whose readings come by broker and whose actions go over HTTP: what `inproc_partners(transport="mqtt")` hands the runner.
A `TimelineSink` that turns events into spans on its own tracer provider (never the process-wide one).
One line per event, for a human watching a scenario run.
A tool was registered twice, named like an actuator, or called with arguments its schema refuses.

The smallest broker that behaves like one for this purpose: topic filters with `+` and `#`, and a persistent session per client, so a message published while the client is away is waiting when it subscribes again (QoS 1 with `clean_session=False`).
An `MqttTransport` onto an `InProcessBroker`.
A small city graph that tests fill with readings and verdicts.
A battery whose loss the test controls. `design` and `held` are functions of the policy; `fails` names a constraint.
A model that fails if it is ever called: replay must not reach it.
Readings from one water-level sensor, numbered like the Twin numbers them.

Normalised word counts over the items' own vocabulary: a word the query shares with an item is the only thing that makes them similar, so which items a search seeds is exactly what the test says it is.
Two harbour gauges in adjacent zones, read once a second, one after the other.
One run of the Brain process against partners that outlive it.
A timeline sink that retracts the evidence of an incident the moment it opens.
A stand-in Twin adapter: three readings, a cursor, a topology.
Stands in for LLMCrew: each role is a coroutine the test supplies; the rest follow the playbook.
Replays a fixed list of assistant messages, as a tool-calling chat model would produce them.
A uvicorn server in a thread, so a test can talk to it over a real socket.
A workspace over the `world` city, with helpers to add incidents of chosen strength.
switch each region off in turn, replay the Test Book, and show what each one is worth
the Brain tunes its own parameters, inside a fence, and shows the evidence

why the Brain decided, or held back, from a saved log: the steps, the gate, what it relied on, what would have changed it

propose the renames and units for a Twin that names things differently (prints; never edits config)
how much solving the dispatch together saves over nearest-first, on random cities (checked against brute force)

attack the Brain 24 ways; every attack must be refused
the whole freeze check, offline: Test Book, baselines, learning curve, ablations, poisoning, screens
run a scenario again and again under injected faults (or against the real model) and report how often the team's plan held
play a run's input journal back into the Brain and check that it decides the same
run a scenario again and report, level by level, what changed: decisions, stream, bytes, prompt
run against the partners configured in config/partners.yaml
run one Test Book scenario against the mocks
run the security invariants and the API edge tests
run the evidence for every threat in docs/SECURITY.md and say which are covered, failing or open
HTTP API, live event stream and timeline screen
learn from stored episodes: promote repeated team plans to reflexes, through a gate
mint a short-lived API token (or --revoke one by id)
run held-out variants of the Test Book (shifted, reseeded, decoyed); each must decide as its base does
check a signed explanation bundle offline: the signature, each log line's own hash, every step's line
check the temporal promises (trust before action, nothing after close, every unit home...) on saved logs or on every scenario
LLM roles as `provider:model` strings (langchain init_chat_model). Groq needs GROQ_API_KEY.
Where the two partner layers live and how to talk to them.
Thresholds and weights. The Academy will tune these; the gate section stays human-owned.
Discovery for other agents: what this Brain offers, how to call it, how to authenticate.
The Brain's public signing keys (EdDSA), so a partner can verify its calls without a shared secret.
High-impact calls waiting for a person (`approval.mode: human`).
The decision's explanation as W3C PROV-JSON.
The city around an incident: zones, nearest facilities, units out, other incidents, sensors. Read live, no identities.

A question about a whole area ("what can the Brain do about flooding, and what is blocked?"): the groups of procedures that answer it, each with a summary written by code from the playbooks and the gate's own policy.
Prometheus text format, computed from the timeline (needs the read scope off loopback).
A person grants or denies one pending approval. A grant puts the held call back through the gate, which checks everything again.
For the Twin and Guardian layers: put your own CloudEvents on the shared timeline.
A person chooses the scripted team (`scripted`) or hands the choice back to the model's own health (`auto`).
For the Guardian: take back a verdict. Later actions that cite the reading stop; sleep forgets what it taught.
The Twin adapter `twin.adapter` names (`mcp`, `http` or `mqtt`), pointed at `twin.url`, with the TLS settings if any.
Trust `ca` (or the system's authorities when none is named) and present `cert` and `key` when given.
The Guardian adapter's HTTP client: verifies the Guardian against `ca`, and presents `cert` when mutual TLS is on.
What `McpTwinAdapter` connects to: the URL as it is, or (for https with TLS settings) a transport that carries them.
The `ssl_*` options for the listener. With `ca` set, a client without a certificate from that authority is refused.
d2 before d10: by the number in the file name, not by its spelling.
What an approval covers: the action, the actuator, the parameters and the incident. The prose of the justification is not part of it.
None when the approval is good for this proposal now; otherwise why not.
Release an embedded Qdrant folder, which only one open client may hold; the next run in the same process needs it.
The knowledge base on Qdrant, answering from an in-memory copy when Qdrant is away. (kb, note); None and a note when it cannot even open.
One line per scenario field that changed. Timings and counts are ignored on purpose.
Run one Test Book scenario and summarise what the Brain read, decided and refused.

config/models.yaml, with the command-line overrides applied.
The partners config for `serve`, with the folders from the command line laid over it.

Play the calm day once, unseen, so the first click on the screen does not wait for the playbook to be embedded.

Check a Twin, a Guardian and a Brain against the contract. No arguments: the shipped mocks and this Brain, in process.
Propose the `twin.type_aliases` and `twin.profiles` for a Twin that names things differently. Prints; never edits a file.

Short stable hash of the behaviour-defining config, stamped on every decision.
Project root: where `config/`, `scenarios/`, `mocks/` and `logs/` live.
Load `config/<name>.yaml` (or an explicit path); fall back to built-in defaults.

A built-in file, or the same-named file in the extra folder when there is one (`rules/` for rules).
What a role's run cost in tokens and calls. Seconds are not here: measured time goes in the event's `timing`.
The read-only tools each role has: the pack's own, and (with `knowledge.team_tools`) the Analyst's three more.

Every pack the Brain knows: the built-in ones, then the folder's. A pack with the same code replaces the earlier one.
The facts in plain words, for the scripted Analyst's summary and the screen.
The rules `brain sleep` promoted, from `rules.yaml` in the learned folder (none if there is no file).
The sightings that count as leaving the scene fast after the crime.
What the other people at the scene did afterwards.

gpt-oss on Groq sometimes gives its final answer through a tool named `json`, which Groq refuses because no such tool was offered. The refusal carries the generation; if it is a complete, valid answer under that name, use it rather than losing the role to its stand-in.
Check the Analyst's citations against the graph.

nodes.summary: Check the Chief's decision against the tool log, the topology, the units and the playbook.

A reliability table on synthetic incidents with a known truth. Witnesses report confidence 0.5 + a signal shifted toward the truth and noise, with a few confidently wrong ones; the table says, for each band of belief, how often the incident was in fact real. This checks that the number is not wildly over- or under-confident for witnesses like these; it says nothing about real witnesses until real data exists.
The cheapest assignment by trying them all (only for small instances).
Breadth-first: every facility in a cut zone is dark, then everything that depends on something dark.
`depends_on: {facility-or-zone: [what it needs]}`. A key or value the topology does not know is rejected, like a pack file.
`feeders: {name: {capacity_kw, zones}}`: zones that share one supply. A zone the topology does not have is rejected.
Every single zone loss, the worst first.

The old rule applied to the same problem, in the order the incidents arrived: the comparison the solver is judged against.
`demands` are in arrival order; `hops(a, b)` is the hop distance or None.
Compare a team's perimeter with the solver's: how many units it uses against the fewest that would do, and the chance the solver's holds.

Why one decision was taken. Raises KeyError for an id the log does not hold.
Why an action was held back. `event_id` is the id of the `brain.action.blocked` event. Raises KeyError for an unknown id.
The story of one incident from its first reading to its close (or to now, if it is still open).
The changes that would have released a held action, from the data of its `brain.action.blocked` event.

(ok, message). Checks the signature, then each line's own hash, then that every step has its line.

One sentence for the caption: at most 25 words.
The Brain's knowledge base as it is deployed (a primary behind a resilient wrapper), with a primary that will stop. The runtime connects `emit`.
One pursuit unit per target, one unit per zone otherwise, one alert per zone, one recall per unit.

The verdict on the first trusted piece of evidence that the incident happened.
The trusted evidence readings, if every one of them is doubted (nothing independent agrees with them).

An overload on a known feeder: disconnect the zones that remove the excess at the least impact, instead of the overloaded zone itself. None when the zone is on no known feeder (the plain rule then applies).

nodes.summary: Proposals for one open non-crime incident, and the dedupe keys of the blocks reported this time.
The trusted reading that shows this person, seen at the scene, leaving it fast. None if there is none.
The records of a journal, after checking the chain line by line and, when a secret is given, the seal.
The journal's copy of one raw reading: as received, without the fields perception dropped or any demographic name.
The `k` communities whose summary reads most like the question (ties by id).
(heading path, paragraph) in file order. Code blocks are left out: they are examples, not prose to retrieve.
Chunks of one document, ids `REF-<NAME>-01`, `-02`, ... A chunk holds paragraphs of one section up to `max_words`; a single paragraph longer than that is kept whole rather than cut mid-sentence.
The configured documents that exist; a missing one is skipped, not an error (the Brain must start without its docs).
Returns (embedder, note). `auto` prefers fastembed and falls back to hashing if it cannot load.
Where the embedding model is kept. fastembed's own default is the system temp directory, which a reboot empties; `FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH` overrides this.

The `k` episodes that read most like this incident (ties by id). An episode of the same kind of incident always comes before one of another kind, whatever the words say: a smog story is a poor guide to a robbery even if both happened in an interior zone.
The kind of place a zone is, without saying which: a city exit, a zone with a facility, an interior zone.
The chance that a question with an answer scores above one without (a tie counts half). 0.5 is no better than chance.

The knowledge base the Brain itself loads at start-up (every department's playbook and rules, the Twin's actuators, the interface card), obtained by starting a calm scenario against the mock partners.

One mode over some questions. `dense` and `keyword` rank with that signal alone; `hybrid` fuses both; `hybrid+graph` also lets the incident type pull in the items linked to it; `graphrag` adds the walk along the playbooks' links.
Recall at 1, 3 and 5 (the share of the expected items found), the reciprocal rank of the first one, and nDCG at 5.
Every mode over the chosen split. `overrides` (`knowledge.mmr`, `knowledge.utility_weight`) are for choosing switches on the design half; with the held-out half in the run they are refused.

nodes.signature: fuse_traced(items, vector_ranked, keyword_ranked, incident_type, department, available_actions, kinds, graph_linked, k, query, scores, mmr, utility_weight, similarity, expansions, seed_scores, decay, conflict_penalty, ranked)
nodes.summary: Reciprocal-rank fusion of the two seed rankings, then graph expansion, with a trace of how it chose.
Nodes are `(kind, name)`: `item`, `incident_type`, `action` and `department`. Every edge has a `rel`.
The items with every unusable link removed, and what was wrong. An item with a bad link stays; only the link goes.

Walk the links from each seed, at most `hops` steps, breadth first, so each item is reached by its shortest path (ties: the path whose ids sort first). Never back to the seed, never through a conflict, and a walk stays in one kind (`GROUPS`).

nodes.signature: graph_seeds(items, vector_ranked, keyword_ranked, department, kinds, n)
nodes.summary: The items the walk starts from, with their search scores: the best `n` of each signal that belong to the right department and kind. One that needs an actuator the Twin lacks is still a seed, because what could stand in for it is what the walk is for.
The BM25 weight of each word in one item. Qdrant multiplies by the word's inverse document frequency (`Modifier.IDF`) at query time.
A stable number for a word, the same on every machine and in every run (Python's own `hash` changes between runs).
Two to four plain questions about one incident: what to do, which procedure applies, and which procedures use what the Twin can do.
Which kind of outage an exception from the model client is. None: not an outage (a bad answer is not a dead model).
One one-token call to a Groq model. Raises ProbeError on a refusal; returns what is left of the limits.
Probe and record the result, so the screen learns of an outage before the next deliberation does.
Keep the SDK's DNS-rebinding protection on: a web page must not be able to call a loopback Brain through the browser.
Run `suite` under each ablation. A learned reflex is taught first (two runs of d3 and one sleep) so that it can be switched off.
Score the tuned overlay on stories nothing was tuned or confirmed on, and retire every value that does not beat the shipped one there.
Take one tuned parameter (or all of them) out of the overlay. The Brain is then exactly the earlier one.
The overlay, and the evidence the Academy wrote down for each value.
Per incident and in total: lit or not, waited how long, and what the slots and the team's runs were spent on.

1 for each configured store that answers right now: Neo4j on its bolt port, a Qdrant server on /readyz (an embedded folder is always up). Neo4j Community has no metrics endpoint of its own, so this is how Prometheus learns whether the City Graph is being kept.

A Brain with tokens required and a low rate limit, attacked from outside its own process boundary (ASGI).
On synthetic streams with a known truth: no spike is ever adopted, a walked threshold still reports the spike, recovery is not doubted.
Variants of the scenarios, shifted in time, with other noise and a decoy sensor, decide as their base does.
Refuse any connection that is not to this machine, and remember each attempt.
Three trusted-looking episodes that all teach a nonsense perimeter must be turned away at rehearsal.
Every scenario's own timeline keeps the temporal promises (trust before action, nothing after close, every unit home).

The city around an incident, as one small graph: where it is, what is near, who is out, what is watching. No person's identity in it.

An explanation in words, over HTTP and from the command line.

The funnel: how many things each stage of attention let through.
GraphRAG: seeds from the hybrid search, then the authored links walked a bounded way, every hit carrying the path that brought it.

The level tracker: a time to the line with an interval, learning only from trusted readings.
Retrieval that can say how it chose: which signals found an item, at what rank, and what was set aside and why.
The links between procedures: written by hand in the playbooks, checked on load, and the graph holds exactly those and no others.
The separation the Phase 1 jury looks for: decision logic never imports a partner protocol, and an adapter imports nothing of the logic.
A plan the team made the same way before, compiled into a reflex: same decisions, no team run.

LLMHealth: a model that stops answering sends the team to its scripted stand-ins at once, and the screen is told why.
Hostile text meets the Brain: ids are refused at the door, values are typed, the gate stops what a fooled model proposes, and a changed Twin tool list is reported.
The Brain as an MCP server: read-only tools, resources and a prompt for other teams' agents, from the same registry our agents use.
Mining: a plan the team made the same way more than once is a candidate lesson. Counting, no model.
The mock Twin's wider actuators: signals, valves and the grid, spoken to as the contract describes.
Coupled sensors: two gauges that should move together. One that drifts alone is disputed, however slowly it drifts.

Packs are files: dropping one into a folder teaches the Brain a new service without touching its code.
The perimeter solver: the fewest units that seal the suspect in, each reaching its zone first, and how likely that is to hold.
The Phase 1 'Required' rules (R1, R2) as tests, so they stay true. See docs/PHASE1-COMPLIANCE.md.
The planning supervisor: the solver goes to the gate first, the team is reconciled when it arrives, a person's approval pauses and resumes it.
When units run out, a named suspect's pursuit may take a perimeter unit from an incident that still has its own pursuit out.
The print-mode figures: standalone, black and white, parseable as XML, and legible at a full landscape page.
The explanation as W3C PROV-JSON: every step an activity, every relation pointing at something defined, the same bytes for the same log.
Qdrant as the vector index: the same answers as the in-memory backend, and a warm start that embeds nothing.
Hybrid search inside Qdrant: dense and keyword searches filtered and fused by the server, agreeing with the Brain's own fusion.
The retrieval evaluation: the metrics are right, the question set is sound, and the held-out half cannot be used to choose anything.
The red team: 24 attacks, each refused, and the kit itself notices when a defence is missing.
The rehearsal: everything the freeze needs, run offline, in one command, with a report.

Reliability of the team: repeated runs, injected faults, and what the verifier and the gate let through.
`brain replay`: the journal of a run is enough to make the Brain decide the same again.
Reproducibility: what a repeated run changes, found by comparing runs, never by assuming.

The knowledge base outlives its index: answers come from the copy, the outage is reported once, recovery is reported, a hang is cut.
A Brain that stops and starts again mid-incident carries on from what it saved.
Retraction: the Guardian takes back a verdict. Later actions that cite the reading stop, and what it taught is revoked.
Salience: a number computed in code from what the Brain can observe, never from a model.
What the new Test Book scenarios rely on: a Twin that goes away and comes back, an index that stops, a renamed Twin, rotated keys, forged pushes.
Scenario baseline streams: a calm day described as a few lines instead of hundreds of events.
End-to-end: the real Brain against the mock Twin (MCP) and mock Guardian (REST), in-process.
Who may call the API: scoped tokens off loopback, size and rate limits, and a push boundary that nobody can speak as the Brain through.
Security claims written as tests, so they stay true: the build fails when one stops holding.

Load shedding: remove at least the excess, at the least impact, exactly (checked against brute force).

TLS and mutual TLS: the listener serves https, refuses a client with no certificate or the wrong authority's, and the adapters connect with the CA and a client certificate.
Short-lived tokens: scoped, audience-bound, expiring, revocable, and never written to an event or a log.
One registry of read-only tools: what our agents call is exactly what a partner's agent will be offered.
Graph algorithms and knowledge retrieval, on the sample city.

nodes.name: fire.respond
nodes.summary: A fire is reported. Send the nearest fire unit to the zone.

nodes.name: accident.respond
nodes.summary: An accident is reported. Send the nearest ambulance to the zone.

nodes.name: jam.signal.green
nodes.summary: Traffic is jammed. Hold the nearest signal on green for two minutes to clear the queue.

nodes.name: police.pursuit.direct
nodes.summary: One person stands out as the suspect of a crime incident. Send a police unit after them.

nodes.name: police.respond.scene
nodes.summary: A crime is corroborated but flight singles no one out, because more than one person left the scene fast. Send one police unit to the scene and name no target.

nodes.name: police.standdown.closed
nodes.summary: The incident is closed. Recall every unit that is still out for it.

nodes.name: police.standdown.outrun
nodes.summary: A trusted sighting places the suspect outside the zones the perimeter was built to hold. Recall the perimeter units so the department can plan again from where the suspect is.

nodes.name: police.standdown.preempted
nodes.summary: A named suspect elsewhere has no unit and the stations are empty. Recall one perimeter unit from an incident whose own pursuit unit is still out, so it can be sent after the suspect who has none.

nodes.name: flood.alert
nodes.summary: A flood is reported. Warn the zone to avoid low-lying roads.

nodes.name: flood.valve.close
nodes.summary: A flood is reported. Close the nearest valve to stop more water entering the zone.

nodes.name: overload.appeal
nodes.summary: A substation is near its capacity. Ask the zone to use less power.

nodes.name: overload.disconnect
nodes.summary: A substation is near its capacity. Ask to disconnect the zone's grid breaker before it fails.

nodes.name: smog.advisory
nodes.summary: The air quality index is high. Advise the zone to limit time outdoors.
